title: 46 Minutes
novel: Lily and Marshall moved to the suburbs, and everything [[changed|change]] for the group. They had been living in the city for years, and the move was a big [[adjustment|adjustment]] for everyone. It took exactly 46 minutes to get from their new house to MacLaren's bar. Ted felt [[abandoned|abandon]] by his best friends. He sat in the apartment and felt the [[silence|silence]] around him. Barney tried to [[distract|distract]] everyone from their sadness. He took the gang to a strip club to [[celebrate|celebrate]] being free from Marshall and Lily's rules. Ted was not in the mood for a party, but he went along anyway. Lily's father [[refused|refuse]] to move out of their new house. He had been living with them and showed no signs of leaving. Marshall tried to [[politely|politely]] ask him to go, but it was no use. Lily's father said he had nowhere else to go and [[begged|beg]] to stay. Marshall and Lily felt [[trapped|trap]] in their own home. They loved Lily's father but needed their own space for the baby. The gang [[gathered|gather]] at MacLaren's and [[realized|realize]] that things would never be the same. Ted said a sad toast to the old days. Barney tried to cheer everyone up but failed. They all felt a sense of [[loss|loss]] that evening, even though they knew the move was for the best.

adjustment.en: getting used to a new situation

abandon.en: to be left behind by others

celebrate.en: to do something special for an event

trap.en: to be stuck in a situation
